sources: https://handbook.monash.edu/2024/courses/E3005 (course requirements, 96 CP from Commerce Parts A+B)

https://www.monash.edu/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/3303641/2024-map-E3005.pdf (course progression map, Electrical and Computer Systems Engineering specialisation, 2024 commencing, updated 14 Oct 2025)
openDecisions: Sahel hasn't decided a major yet (still applying to the double degree) — shortlisted 4: Finance, Economics, Business Analytics, Econometrics. All 4 are researched and added below as explorable options so he can compare progress; he'll only actually complete ONE of these 48cp blocks.

Each `unit` now carries a `major` field: "core" (Part A, everyone), "finance", "economics", "business-analytics", or "econometrics" — used to group the sidebar into per-major sections. A handful of units are required/optional in more than one major (see their `notes`) but only carry ONE `major` tag here (their strongest/first-researched role) to keep sidebar grouping simple.

Per major, only CORE (mandatory) units and small/closed elective pools (roughly ≤12 options) are listed as real catalog entries. Economics' own elective pool ('Economics units offered at Clayton', 24cp from ~30+ units across 6 overlapping themes) is NOT enumerated — it's too large and open-ended to usefully list as catalog cards. Add specific Economics electives as custom units once actually chosen.

year/semester for every Part B (major) unit below is Claude's suggested placement, not an authoritative Handbook sequence — Monash doesn't mandate a specific semester for major electives, only a level-1/2/3 credit-point mix. Placement follows this reasoning: Level 1/2 major units → Year 3 (matches the E3005 map's un-suffixed 'Commerce listed major unit 1/2/3' slots); Level 3 units → Year 4 or Year 5 ('3rd year level' slots on the map), ordered to respect real prerequisite chains found during research. Treat these as a reasonable starting sequence to edit, not fact.

Real prerequisite chains exist WITHIN majors that aren't obvious from unit titles: Finance's BFC2751/BFC3241 (and several electives) need BFC2140 (Corporate finance) first; several Finance electives need BOTH BFC2140 AND BFC2751; Economics' ECC2010 needs BOTH ECC1000 AND ECC1100; all four Econometrics 'Level 3' units need ETC2410 first; Business Analytics' ETC3250 needs ETC2420, and ETC3555/FIT3003 go a level deeper still.

Cross-major overlaps found: ETC2410 is Finance-major CORE but also a Business Analytics elective option and effectively feeds the whole Econometrics major. ECC2000/ECC2010 are Economics-major core but also count as Econometrics elective options. ETC2420/ETC3250 are Business Analytics core but also Econometrics elective options. ETC3460 is a Finance elective AND one of the Econometrics 'choose 3 of 4' Level-3 units. These are each entered ONCE (see the `major` field note above) with both roles documented in `notes`.

FIT2094 and FIT3171 (both 'Databases', a Business Analytics elective option) are a REAL prohibition pair — same content at Level 2 vs Level 3, only one may be counted. First genuine prohibition-conflict pair in the catalog data itself (previously only tested with synthetic custom units).

FIT3171 and FIT3179 (both Business Analytics electives) list ENG1003/ENG1013/ENG1014 as valid alternative prerequisites — units this student already has from the Electrical catalog — so those two may already be unlocked without needing FIT1045 first.

Gap found: FIT3154 (Business Analytics elective 'Advanced data analysis') requires FIT2086 'Modelling for data analysis', which isn't offered anywhere in this catalog or major list. It'll show a permanent 'prerequisite isn't in your plan' flag unless FIT2086 is added as a custom unit — flagging here rather than silently omitting FIT3154, since it's still a real elective option.

Some Finance elective units are NOT standard Clayton semester units even though the Handbook lists them under the major: BFX3301 (Treasury and financial markets) is Caulfield-only, taught in a quota-limited trading-simulation lab; BFX3871 (International study program in banking and finance) is an overseas summer immersion block with its own extra costs; BEX3726 (a Business Analytics elective) is a similar Term-1 immersion block requiring 72cp completed first. Left in the catalog since they're real options, but flagged in their notes.

Part A also includes an 'Additional commerce unit' (6 CP, flexible/FREE-eligible) and one 'Capstone, consulting project, international experience or internship unit' (6 CP, chosen from ~30 options, sits in Year 4 Semester 2 on the ECE course map) — neither has a fixed code, so neither is listed as a catalog unit here. Add whichever specific unit is chosen as a custom unit closer to the time.

ACC1100 vs ACC1001: only one counts toward the 36 CP Part A core. ACC1100 is required if majoring in Accounting or Actuarial Studies; otherwise either satisfies the requirement. Both listed as separate catalog entries — add whichever one applies, not both.

ECC1000 vs ECX2953: only one counts. ECX2953 is restricted to students completing an Accounting major in a double degree (E3005 is on its approved-course list) and is required for professional accounting accreditation; ECC1000 is the standard choice for every other major. Both listed as separate catalog entries.

The E3005 double-degree course map places several ECE core units in different semesters than the E3007 single-degree map already in electrical.json (e.g. ECE2191 and ECE4132 move from Year 2/5 to Year 3 Semester 2; ECE3141 moves from Year 5 to Year 4 Semester 1; an extra 'Level 4/5 ECE-coded core elective' slot appears in Year 4 Semester 1). electrical.json was NOT changed to match, since Sahel's transfer to the double degree isn't confirmed yet and the current single-degree placements are what's actually enrolled. If the transfer is confirmed, electrical.json's year/semester fields should be updated to the E3005 sequence.

Part B major units are SUGGESTED placements: the map only says "Commerce listed major unit 1..8" across Y3S1-Y5S1, so each unit's SEMESTER here is its real Clayton offering but which major slot it fills is the student's choice.
_meta.vintagePolicy: Unit facts track the CURRENT Handbook (requisites apply from the year you enrol in the unit); course structure tracks the 2025 commencing year. Re-check with: node scripts/check-vintage-drift.mjs --from 2025 --codes-from data/commerce.json
_meta.requisiteNote: Requisites are conjunctive GROUPS: prerequisiteText carries the full Handbook expression and the prerequisites array lists ONE representative per required group. Two units in the whole catalog (FIT2094 here, ENG1013 in common-first-year.json) have a rule shaped OR-of-AND, which a flat array cannot represent - both carry an explicit RULE LOGIC NOTE. The harvester flags these with groupsAreLossy so they cannot pass unnoticed again.
